title: Affine linearization identifies the specified units and ideal-module cokernels
statement: For any scheme X [def-pc-scheme] and j≥0, let e_j:E_(j+1)→E_j be the constructed inclusion of [lem-sc-reduction-units-power-inclusion], and let F_j be the constructed quasi-coherent module cokernel of [lem-sc-reduction-ideal-power-quotient]. There is an isomorphism coker(e_j) ≅ ULift((F_j)_et) of abelian sheaves on the small etale site of X [def-sc-etale-qcoherent-module]. All cokernels and F_j are specified constructions.

source.place: Proof, Step 1 and the following Claim; proof text retained in the parent DAG node

proof.text: Over an affine etale object V→U=Spec A, write B=Γ(V,O_V), I=N(U)^(j+1), J=N(U)^(j+2). The affine base-change description of the two closed subschemes identifies the kernels E_j(V), E_(j+1)(V) with the units 1+IB, 1+JB. The constructed inclusion is the ordinary inclusion because it commutes with their inclusions into Gm. Flatness and the affine ideal-module and module-cokernel descriptions identify Γ(V,V^*F_j) with IB/JB, compatibly with restriction.

Define on these affine objects 1+a↦a mod JB. Multiplication gives a+b+ab, and ab∈JB because 2j+2≥j+2. The kernel is 1+JB. Every class lifts to a∈IB, and a is nilpotent: it is a finite sum of multiples of nilpotent elements from N(U). Thus 1+a is a unit (inverse given by the finite geometric sum), proving surjectivity.

Pullback of functions carries a to its ring image, so the maps commute with restriction. Affine etale refinements cover the small etale site, hence the maps glue to a sheaf morphism whose kernel is the specified inclusion and which is locally surjective. It has the cokernel universal property; uniqueness of cokernels gives the isomorphism. Lifting the additive groups sectionwise preserves this comparison. For N=0 or empty X both sides vanish; for j=0 the cross-term inequality is equality.
